conventions: effects.contract.willingnessDelta: signed points, positive = MORE willing to re-sign with this club. Wire it into ContractNegotiationEngine.situationBreakdown (:974-983) as one new .lifeEvent Source component whose value = -willingnessDelta/100 (that array's convention is positive value = costs more), then let the existing 0.72...1.50 clamp bound it. effects.performance.focusDebuff: signed points on EFFECTIVE ratings only — never on trueOverall, never fog-revealing. Positive values are buffs. effects.motivation.set: a MotivationState rawValue. '.distracted' is a NEW case (developmentMultiplier ~0.70, moraleDelta -2, focusGainMultiplier ~0.80); adding it is free per c1 §8.1 rule 4 because Player.motivationStateRaw is an optional String column. Because MotivationState is recomputed wholesale each trainingCamp, any in-season set MUST carry its own duration counter in LifeEventsState. Hold-in vs holdout: a HOLD-IN must NOT set Player.isHoldingOut (that flag hard-excludes the player from GameSimulator, LiveGameEngine, attendance, development and trade targeting) — he is available on Sunday and only loses practice. A true HOLDOUT does set it, via HoldoutEngine.startHoldout. No event writes contract money directly: every monetary resolution routes through DealTargetYear.plan + verdict so the cap gate and the booking cannot drift (#186). userTeamOnly = true means the event still occurs league-wide for simulation purposes but only surfaces in the feed when it lands on the user's club. PLACEHOLDERS: the schema's core set ({PLAYER} {POS} {TEAM} {CITY} {COACH} {AGE} {SPOUSE}) plus six numeric/label fills this file needs — {N} (remaining weeks, games, yards or count, resolved by context), {YEAR} (league year), {COUNT} (ordinal, e.g. third nomination), {FINE} (accrued fine total), {RECORD} (club record at fire time) and {ROUND} (draft round). All six appear only where a number is the point. ONE DOCUMENTED DEVIATION from schema rule 5: moderate-tier POSITIVE ceremony beats (milestone reached, ring of honour, jersey proceeds, comeback, final home game) use surface=popup without carrying a decision. Rule 5's 'popup only if it carries a decision' is read as governing negative severity — a celebration the coach should not be able to scroll past is a blocking sheet by intent. Every moderate NEGATIVE popup in this file carries a real decision; that half of the rule is enforced by the build validator.

targetLeagueYearVolume.notes: Sum of every expectedPerLeagueYear in this file. The structural positive templates (32 community nominees, 32 first-time captains, 28 foundation launches, 24 mentorships) dominate the raw total by design — they are per-club calendar certainties from r3 §6.1/§9.5, not rolls, and all are marked userTeamOnly so the coach's feed sees his own club's drip rather than 32 copies of it.

calibrationSummary: K3 reconciles to the r3 base rates family by family (league = 32 clubs, ~69 players each). HOLD-IN/HOLDOUT 7.35/yr vs r3 §5.1 '3-8 notable holdouts/hold-ins per league-year' — inside band, weighted to the hold-in because the 2020 mandatory non-waivable camp fine made the true holdout the minority tactic; two of the seven templates (intensity downgrade, fine-ledger notice) are escalation beats on an already active standoff and are counted here rather than hidden. TRADE REQUESTS 4.5/yr vs r3 §5.2 '2-5 public requests per league-year' and the K3 brief's 3-6 star-tier sagas — sits at the shared midpoint; the superstar-saga template alone is 0.8/yr, matching '1-3 reach national saga status'. FRANCHISE TAG 8.2/yr across four templates against an [E] base of 8-12 tags per league-year, i.e. roughly 0.7 tag-related news beats per tag. CAMP FIGHTS 42.1/yr vs r3 §5.5 '30-60 reported camp fights per league-year' — inside band; the national slice (national item + star-vs-star + rookie + brawl = 12.7) matches '5-15 become national items', and the discipline slice (ejection 3.0 + league fine 0.4) matches '1-3 produce discipline or fines'. SIDELINE BLOWUPS 12.5/yr vs r3 §5.4 '8-20 nationally-covered sideline incidents per league-year'. ANONYMOUS SOURCE 14.0/yr vs r3 §5.9 '10-25 per league-year'; the player-directed slice alone is 4.0/yr, which is the K3 brief's 4-8 band — the brief scoped only the player-directed stories, r3 counts the coach-directed and preseason genres too, so both numbers are satisfied at once. The weeks 8-14 / below-expectation gate in contextRule is what produces the research's concentration on bottom-quartile clubs; the template is hard-suppressed above .700. OLD POSTS RESURFACING 3.7/yr vs r3 §5.7 '2-6 per league-year, overwhelmingly at the draft' — the draft-eve variant carries 68% of it. LIVESTREAM 1.6/yr vs r3 §5.8 '1-3 per league-year'. PODCAST/INTERVIEW 5.5/yr vs r3 §5.6 '3-8 per league-year'. POSITIVES are structural, not probabilistic, per r3 §9.5: community award nominees are exactly 32.0/yr because every club nominates exactly one player every December (r3 §6.1), finalists 3.0 and winner exactly 1.0; foundation launches 28.0/yr against r3 §6.2's '20-40 per league-year'; the philanthropy family totals 33.1/yr with the viral mega-fund at 0.8 against '0-2 per league-year, tightly coupled to a disaster' — hence the coupled k3_regional_disaster_trigger, which is the only way the viral template can fire. Captaincy (32.0 first-time + 20.0 repeat) and mentorship (24.0) are likewise structural per-club rates, not rolls. FILE TOTAL 574.45 expected events per league-year, of which 185.15 surface league-wide and 389.3 are userTeamOnly — so the coach's actual feed sees roughly 185.15 K3 items per season league-wide plus his own club's structural drip, well inside the ~20-40 items/season budget rule 4 protects. Positive + milestone = 43/113 events (38%), matching the K3 brief's 35-40% requirement and exceeding the schema's 15-25% floor because this file carries the design's positive weight.

events.title: Anonymous Sources: The Room Has Lost Faith in a Player
events.headline: Report: teammates have 'stopped counting on' {PLAYER}

probability.calibration: r3 §5.9 [V]: 10-25 anonymous-source stories per league-year concentrated on losing records and hot-seat coaches; the K3 brief scopes the player-directed slice at 4-8/yr. This is that slice at its midpoint.

events.designNotes: The anatomy is fixed: report -> denial -> teammate-support quotes -> 2-5 day arc -> fades or becomes the epitaph. Build the denial and support beats into the arc so the coach sees the whole shape.
events.contextRule: Fires only in weeks 8-14 AND only when the club's win percentage trails its preseason projected win total by 2.0 wins or more. Weight scales with the shortfall: -2.0 wins = 1.0x, -4.0 = 2.2x, -6.0 = 3.5x. Suppressed entirely at teamWinPct >= .700 (the research finds these stories almost never appear on a 12-win team).

events.title: Community Award Nominee
events.headline: {TEAM} names {PLAYER} its community award nominee
events.body: Each club nominates exactly one player for the league's community award, and {TEAM} chose {PLAYER}. The nomination carries a donation to the causes he works with and a week of local coverage he has spent eight years quietly earning. He thanked, by name, a woman who runs a food bank in {CITY}.

probability.calibration: r3 §6.1/T19 [V]: STRUCTURAL — all 32 clubs nominate exactly one player every December, guaranteeing 32 positive local stories per league-year. This is not a probability; it is a calendar certainty (one per club).

eligibility.notes: Any tier. Raises this player's community-award nomination weight by 2.0x permanently.

events.title: League Hall of Legends Induction
events.headline: {PLAYER} is inducted into the league's hall of legends
events.body: Five years after his final snap, {PLAYER} was inducted with four others. He was presented by the coach who drafted him, which had been arranged eleven months in advance and kept quiet the entire time.

probability.calibration: [E]: the league's highest career honour, ~3-8 inductees per year; modeled at 3.0 to keep the honour scarce in a long dynasty save. Fictional analog only — never the real institution or its city.

eligibility.notes: Requires a retired player five years past his final season with a career legacy threshold. League-wide event.

events.designNotes: The top of the legacy ladder. Milestones, community awards and championships should all feed one legacy score that decides induction, so the positive events in this file compound across decades.

playerCard.detailLine: Inducted into the league's hall of legends, {YEAR}

events.title: First Career Score
events.headline: {PLAYER} scores his first, and the ball is already in a bag
events.body: The rookie handed it off on the way to the sideline without being told to. Somebody on the equipment staff had the bag out before he reached the bench. His mother was in section 118.

probability.calibration: r3 §6.3 [V]: the preserved first-score ball is a documented recurring beat; [E] ~16 per league-year across rookie classes reach even local coverage. userTeamOnly.

eligibility.notes: Rookies and second-year players only, first career score.

events.designNotes: Cheap, frequent, and it attaches an emotional marker to a rookie the coach might otherwise experience as a row in a table.

events.title: A Veteran's Final Home Game
events.headline: {TEAM} sends {PLAYER} off in {CITY}
events.body: He announced two weeks ago that this would be his last season, and the club did the thing properly: a tribute in the third quarter, his family on the field afterward, and a standing ovation that went on long enough to be uncomfortable and then long enough to be moving.

probability.calibration: r3 §6.3 [V]: the send-off is part of the documented milestone-and-return family; [E] ~2 per league-year at ceremony scale.

eligibility.notes: Requires an announced retirement and 6+ seasons with the club.

events.designNotes: Closes the loop the mentor and captain templates open. A career that accumulated positives should end with a scene, not with a roster transaction line.
